Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Acute left-sided throbbing headache with nausea, vomiting x2, photophobia, visual aura (“zig-zag lines,” blurred vision) – consistent with migraine (second episode in one month).  
  • Work-related stress.  
  • Combined oral contraceptive pill (Microgynon) – potential hormonal migraine trigger.
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Mother: migraines, hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).  
  • No known family history of brain tumor or other neurological disease.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Previously self-treated migraine with unspecified “painkillers.”  
  • Recommended today: acetaminophen, co-codamol, ibuprofen or naproxen (doses/frequencies not documented).
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • On oral contraceptive for contraception (3 months).  
  • No other sexual health details recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • Does not exercise; no dietary information recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Denies smoking.  
  • Denies alcohol use.  
  • No other substance use recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  • Reports significant work-related stress.  
  • Denies low mood; no self-harm ideation.
- Vision problems or recent changes:
  • Blurred vision and visual aura preceding headache; photophobia.  
  • No baseline vision status recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives alone.  
  • Works in fashion industry; high job stress.  
  • No caring responsibilities documented.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Provided education and reassurance that presentation most consistent with migraine; low likelihood of brain tumor or meningitis.
- Advised acute treatment options: acetaminophen, co-codamol, NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen).
- Recommended maintaining a headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.
- Discussed possibility of prophylactic migraine medication if headaches persist; to re-evaluate at follow-up next week.
- Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if headache worsens, fails to improve in 2–3 days, develops neurological deficits, progressive neck pain, or visual changes.
- Follow-up appointment: next week.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, HR), BMI, basic neurological and fundoscopic examination findings, immunisation review, alcohol units/week quantification, smoking pack-years (even if none), diet details, mental health screening tool (e.g., K-10), cervical screening status, STI screening, fasting glucose/lipids, urine dipstick.  
● Internal contradictions: None significant; clinician mentioned “Lyme’s disease” though patient did not—unclear context.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor incomplete sentences but clinical content understandable.
